name: Apapa Port (Lagos)
summary: Nigeria's busiest seaport complex; handles most national container traffic.
description: Apapa and neighbouring Tin Can Island (TCIP) are the Lagos port cluster under the Nigerian Ports Authority, with private terminal operators. Congestion on the Apapa–Oshodi corridor has been a chronic logistics bottleneck. The ports remain the primary import gateway for the southwest and much of the north.
economy: Containers, bulk, tank farms, trucking, bonded terminals.
significance: National import hub, Apapa Wharf, Tin Can Island.

name: Port Harcourt Port
summary: Oil and general cargo port on the Bonny River up from the Atlantic.
description: Port Harcourt's port (and nearby Onne) serve eastern Nigeria and the oil industry. Draft and dredging limit some vessel classes compared with Lagos; oil-service boats dominate. The city grew around this harbour from 1912.
economy: Oil export support, general cargo, eastern hinterland.
significance: Garden City harbour, Onne satellite, eastern gateway.

name: Calabar Port
summary: Deep-water port on the Cross River estuary serving the southeast and Cameroon trade.
description: Calabar has been a seaport since the Efik city-state era. The modern port handles general cargo and has been promoted for export processing. Silting and channel maintenance are recurring issues.
economy: General cargo, regional export, limited cruise/tourism.

name: Warri Port
summary: Delta port for oil, steel, and agricultural hinterland cargoes.
description: Warri Port on the Warri River serves the western delta industrial belt including the refinery and steel-related traffic. Access is via dredged delta channels toward Escravos.
economy: Oil products, general cargo, delta logistics.

name: Onne Port
summary: Modern deep-water complex east of Port Harcourt; largest Nigerian port by land area.
description: Onne (Federal Ocean Terminal / Federal Lighter Terminal and oil-and-gas free zone) was developed for energy logistics: rigs, pipes, and project cargo. It complements congested Lagos for specialised energy shipments.
economy: Oil services, free zone, project cargo, containers (growing).
significance: Energy logistics hub, free zone, large land take.
